observations: A large stack of retail boxes for car batteries.
The brand 'THUNDERMAX' is printed on all visible boxes.
Model 'CMF 57512 DIN75' with '12V 75Ah' is visible on the left and center stacks in photo 0.
Model 'CMF 60038 DIN100' with '12V 100Ah' is visible on the right stack in photo 0.
The boxes appear sealed, but no individual batteries are visible outside their packaging.

claims.evidence: Quality cannot be determined from photos of boxes; requires load testing and usage history.

claims.claim: made from korea,Malaysia, Vietnam and Chinese etc
claims.evidence: The specific country of origin for these units is not legible on the boxes from this distance.

risks.risk: The boxes may be empty or contain used/different batteries.
risks.proof: A photo of an open box showing the battery inside.

risks.risk: The batteries may be old stock (expired shelf life) and unable to hold a charge.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the manufacturing date code stamped on the battery casing.

risks.risk: The batteries may be discharged below the point of recovery.
risks.proof: A video showing a multimeter reading of at least 12.6V.

proof_requests: Photo of a battery outside the box showing the top terminals and labels.
Close-up of the manufacturing date stamp on the battery body.
Video of a voltage test using a multimeter.
response.reason: The brand and specific models (75Ah and 100Ah) are clearly identified from the retail packaging. The item can be priced at its worst-case (scrap/dead) until health and contents are proven.
